title: Learning trumpet, the chapel orchestra, and his father's cornet days
summary: He learned trumpet from his father, who taught scales, played in a church chapel orchestra, and had played cornet in Texas in King Oliver's era.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well, oh you learned to play piano first?
You told me once that your father played tuba.

He did when I, when, as he got older. He gradually got away from that cornet and when I was learning trumpet, which he taught me, the scales, but I already knew how to read from playing piano. And we had a chapel orchestra that played for churches, funerals and social affairs in the park on Sunday afternoons and we rehearsed at my house, every Sunday. And my dad played tuba then.

Me and, there were three trumpets and my father was on the bass at that time. You see, but earlier during the years like when King Oliver was in New Orleans, my dad was in Texas playing trumpet, cornet, rather.
Well was he sort of playing in the equivalent of jazz orchestras at that time?
But not when I knew him. I mean that was before I was born. You see, my dad was playing at the same time King Oliver was playing.
Well what sort of bands, were there any that you ever heard of?
No. You see, Texas was a little, wasn't New Orleans. Everything was centered around New Orleans. But there were always good musicians in Texas, you see.
